passages.text: At the end of every seven years you must cancel debts.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel a law.
God commanded them to cancel debts.
They must do this at the end of every seven years.
This law is called the year of release.
passages.original: מִקֵּ֥ץ שֶֽׁבַע־ שָׁנִ֖ים תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה שְׁמִטָּֽה׃

passages.text: This is the manner of remission: Every creditor shall cancel what he has loaned to his neighbor. He is not to collect anything from his neighbor or brother, because the LORD’s time of release has been proclaimed.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to practice remission of debts.
Every creditor must cancel what he has loaned to his neighbor.
The creditor must not collect anything from his neighbor.
The creditor must not collect anything from his brother.
The LORD has proclaimed a time of release.
This time of release belongs to the LORD.
passages.original: וְזֶה֮ דְּבַ֣ר הַשְּׁמִטָּה֒ שָׁמ֗וֹט כָּל־ בַּ֙עַל֙ מַשֵּׁ֣ה יָד֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַשֶּׁ֖ה בְּרֵעֵ֑הוּ לֹֽא־ יִגֹּ֤שׂ אֶת־ רֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ וְאֶת־ אָחִ֔יו כִּֽי־ קָרָ֥א שְׁמִטָּ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You may collect something from a foreigner, but you must forgive whatever your brother owes you.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel a law about debts.
God told Israel to forgive debts every seven years.
God said, “You may collect what a foreigner owes you.”
God said, “You must forgive what your fellow Israelite owes you.”
passages.original: אֶת־ הַנָּכְרִ֖י תִּגֹּ֑שׂ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ אֶת־ אָחִ֖יךָ תַּשְׁמֵ֥ט יָדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: There will be no poor among you, however, because the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess as an inheritance, if only you obey the LORD your God and are careful to follow all these commandments I am giving you today.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
God gives you the land.
God gives you this land as your inheritance.
God will surely bless you in this land.
There will be no poor among you.
This will happen if you obey the LORD your God.
You must listen to His voice.
You must carefully follow all the commandments I give you today.
passages.original: אֶ֕פֶס כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה־ בְּךָ֖ אֶבְי֑וֹן כִּֽי־ בָרֵ֤ךְ יְבָֽרֶכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה בָּאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹֽתֵן־ לְךָ֥ נַחֲלָ֖ה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃ רַ֚ק אִם־ שָׁמ֣וֹעַ תִּשְׁמַ֔ע בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לִשְׁמֹ֤ר לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַמִּצְוָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: When the LORD your God blesses you as He has promised, you will lend to many nations but borrow from none; you will rule over many nations but be ruled by none.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD will bless you.
The LORD promised to bless you.
You will lend to many nations.
You will not borrow from any nation.
You will rule over many nations.
No nation will rule over you.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ בֵּֽרַכְךָ֔ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּר־ לָ֑ךְ וְהַֽעֲבַטְתָּ֞ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֗ים וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א תַעֲבֹ֔ט וּמָֽשַׁלְתָּ֙ בְּגוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים וּבְךָ֖ לֹ֥א יִמְשֹֽׁלוּ׃ס

passages.text: If there is a poor man among your brothers within any of the gates in the land that the LORD your God is giving you, then you are not to harden your heart or shut your hand from your poor brother.
passages.sermon:
God is giving you a land to possess.
You live in this land.
You have brothers among your people.
If one of your brothers becomes poor,
He lives in one of your towns.
Do not harden your heart toward your poor brother.
Do not close your hand against your poor brother.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִהְיֶה֩ בְךָ֨ אֶבְי֜וֹן מֵאַחַ֤ד אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד שְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ בְּאַ֨רְצְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁר־ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֣ן לָ֑ךְ לֹ֧א תְאַמֵּ֣ץ אֶת־ לְבָבְךָ֗ וְלֹ֤א תִקְפֹּץ֙ אֶת־ יָ֣דְךָ֔ מֵאָחִ֖יךָ הָאֶבְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Instead, you are to open your hand to him and freely loan him whatever he needs.
passages.sermon:
God commands you to help your fellow Israelite who is poor.
You must open your hand to him.
You must not hold back from him.
You must lend him what he needs.
You must give him enough to cover his lack.
You must provide for whatever he is missing.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ פָתֹ֧חַ תִּפְתַּ֛ח אֶת־ יָדְךָ֖ ל֑וֹ וְהַעֲבֵט֙ תַּעֲבִיטֶ֔נּוּ דֵּ֚י מַחְסֹר֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֶחְסַ֖ר לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Be careful not to harbor this wicked thought in your heart: “The seventh year, the year of release, is near,” so that you look upon your poor brother begrudgingly and give him nothing. He will cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel a law about helping the poor.
God commanded the people not to be selfish or hard-hearted.
Do not let an evil thought grow in your heart.
Do not say, “The seventh year, the year of release, is near.”
Do not use this as an excuse to refuse your poor brother.
Do not look at your poor brother with a grudging eye.
Do not withhold help from him.
If you refuse to help, your poor brother may cry out to the LORD against you.
If he cries out, you will be guilty of sin.
passages.original: הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֡ פֶּן־ יִהְיֶ֣ה דָבָר֩ עִם־ לְבָבְךָ֨ בְלִיַּ֜עַל לֵאמֹ֗ר קָֽרְבָ֣ה שְׁנַֽת־ הַשֶּׁבַע֮ שְׁנַ֣ת הַשְּׁמִטָּה֒ וְרָעָ֣ה עֵֽינְךָ֗ בְּאָחִ֙יךָ֙ הָֽאֶבְי֔וֹן וְלֹ֥א תִתֵּ֖ן ל֑וֹ וְקָרָ֤א עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה בְךָ֖ חֵֽטְא׃

passages.text: Give generously to him, and do not let your heart be grieved when you do so. And because of this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything to which you put your hand.
passages.sermon:
God commands you to give to the poor and needy.
Give to him freely.
Do not feel sad or upset when you give to him.
Give with a willing heart.
Because you do this, the LORD your God will bless you.
God will bless you in all your work.
God will bless everything you do.
passages.original: נָת֤וֹן תִּתֵּן֙ ל֔וֹ וְלֹא־ יֵרַ֥ע לְבָבְךָ֖ בְּתִתְּךָ֣ ל֑וֹ כִּ֞י בִּגְלַ֣ל׀ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה יְבָרֶכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכָֽל־ מַעֲשֶׂ֔ךָ וּבְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁלַ֥ח יָדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: For there will never cease to be poor in the land; that is why I am commanding you to open wide your hand to your brother and to the poor and needy in your land.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God says there will always be poor people in the land.
God commands the people to help others.
God tells them to open their hand to their brother.
God tells them to give to the poor in their land.
God tells them to give to the needy in their land.
passages.original: כִּ֛י לֹא־ יֶחְדַּ֥ל אֶבְי֖וֹן מִקֶּ֣רֶב הָאָ֑רֶץ עַל־ כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר פָּ֠תֹחַ תִּפְתַּ֨ח אֶת־ יָדְךָ֜ לְאָחִ֧יךָ לַעֲנִיֶּ֛ךָ וּלְאֶבְיֹנְךָ֖ בְּאַרְצֶֽךָ׃ס

passages.text: If a fellow Hebrew, a man or a woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, then in the seventh year you must set him free.
passages.sermon:
A fellow Hebrew may be sold to you.
This person may be a man or a woman.
He or she will serve you for six years.
In the seventh year, you must set this person free.
You must release him or her from your service.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִמָּכֵ֨ר לְךָ֜ אָחִ֣יךָ הָֽעִבְרִ֗י א֚וֹ הָֽעִבְרִיָּ֔ה וַעֲבָֽדְךָ֖ שֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים וּבַשָּׁנָה֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔ת תְּשַׁלְּחֶ֥נּוּ חָפְשִׁ֖י מֵעִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: And when you release him, do not send him away empty-handed.
passages.sermon: When you set your servant free, do not let him leave with nothing.\r\nGive him something when he goes.\r\nDo not send him away empty-handed.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ תְשַׁלְּחֶ֥נּוּ חָפְשִׁ֖י מֵֽעִמָּ֑ךְ לֹ֥א תְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ רֵיקָֽם׃

passages.text: You are to furnish him liberally from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. You shall give to him as the LORD your God has blessed you.
passages.sermon:
God commands you to be generous to your Hebrew servant when you set him free.
Give to him from your flock.
Give to him from your threshing floor.
Give to him from your winepress.
Give to him as much as the LORD your God has blessed you.
Share your blessings with him.
passages.original: הַעֲנֵ֤יק תַּעֲנִיק֙ ל֔וֹ מִצֹּ֣אנְךָ֔ וּמִֽגָּרְנְךָ֖ וּמִיִּקְבֶ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר בֵּרַכְךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ תִּתֶּן־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you; that is why I am giving you this command today.
passages.sermon: You were once slaves in the land of Egypt.\r\nThe LORD your God redeemed you from slavery.\r\nThis is why I give you this command today.
passages.original: וְזָכַרְתָּ֗ כִּ֣י עֶ֤בֶד הָיִ֙יתָ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַֽיִּפְדְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ עַל־ כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֧י מְצַוְּךָ֛ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: But if your servant says to you, ‘I do not want to leave you,’ because he loves you and your household and is well off with you, then take an awl and pierce it through his ear into the door, and he will become your servant for life. And treat your maidservant the same way.
passages.sermon:
A servant may live in your house.
He may serve you.
He may serve your family.
He may say to you, “I do not want to leave you.”
He may say this because he loves you.
He may love your household.
He may be happy with you.
If he says this, you must do something.
Take an awl.
Place his ear against the door.
Pierce his ear with the awl.
He will become your servant for life.
Do the same for your female servant.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־ יֹאמַ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ לֹ֥א אֵצֵ֖א מֵעִמָּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י אֲהֵֽבְךָ֙ וְאֶת־ בֵּיתֶ֔ךָ כִּי־ ט֥וֹב ל֖וֹ עִמָּֽךְ׃ וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ אֶת־ הַמַּרְצֵ֗עַ וְנָתַתָּ֤ה בְאָזְנוֹ֙ וּבַדֶּ֔לֶת וְהָיָ֥ה לְךָ֖ עֶ֣בֶד עוֹלָ֑ם וְאַ֥ף לַאֲמָתְךָ֖ תַּעֲשֶׂה־ כֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Do not regard it as a hardship to set your servant free, because his six years of service were worth twice the wages of a hired hand. And the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to the Israelites.
God told them to set their servants free after six years of service.
Do not think it is hard to let your servant go free.
Your servant worked for you for six years.
His work was worth twice as much as a hired worker.
The LORD your God will bless you in everything you do.
passages.original: לֹא־ יִקְשֶׁ֣ה בְעֵינֶ֗ךָ בְּשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ֙ אֹת֤וֹ חָפְשִׁי֙ מֵֽעִמָּ֔ךְ כִּ֗י מִשְׁנֶה֙ שְׂכַ֣ר שָׂכִ֔יר עֲבָֽדְךָ֖ שֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים וּבֵֽרַכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃פ

passages.text: You must set apart to the LORD your God every firstborn male produced by your herds and flocks. You are not to put the firstborn of your oxen to work, nor are you to shear the firstborn of your flock.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to Israel.
God said, “Set apart every firstborn male from your herds and flocks for Me.”
Give every firstborn male animal to the LORD your God.
Do not use the firstborn ox from your herd for work.
Do not shear the firstborn sheep from your flock.
passages.original: כָּֽל־ הַבְּכ֡וֹר אֲשֶׁר֩ יִוָּלֵ֨ד בִּבְקָרְךָ֤ וּבְצֹֽאנְךָ֙ הַזָּכָ֔ר תַּקְדִּ֖ישׁ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹ֤א תַעֲבֹד֙ בִּבְכֹ֣ר שׁוֹרֶ֔ךָ וְלֹ֥א תָגֹ֖ז בְּכ֥וֹר צֹאנֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Each year you and your household are to eat it before the LORD your God in the place the LORD will choose.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
God will choose a special place.
You must go to that place each year.
You and your household must eat the offering there.
You must do this before the LORD your God.
passages.original: לִפְנֵי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֤יךָ תֹאכֲלֶ֙נּוּ֙ שָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֔ה בַּמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ יִבְחַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אַתָּ֖ה וּבֵיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But if an animal has a defect, is lame or blind, or has any serious flaw, you must not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for sacrifices.
God required animals for sacrifice to be without defects.
If an animal has a defect, do not sacrifice it.
If an animal is lame, do not sacrifice it.
If an animal is blind, do not sacrifice it.
If an animal has any serious flaw, do not sacrifice it.
You must not offer any defective animal to the LORD your God.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִהְיֶ֨ה ב֜וֹ מ֗וּם פִּסֵּ֙חַ֙ א֣וֹ עִוֵּ֔ר כֹּ֖ל מ֣וּם רָ֑ע לֹ֣א תִזְבָּחֶ֔נּוּ לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Eat it within your gates; both the ceremonially unclean and clean may eat it as they would a gazelle or a deer.
passages.sermon:
You may eat the animal within your gates.
Anyone may eat it.
A person who is ceremonially unclean may eat it.
A person who is ceremonially clean may also eat it.
They may eat it together.
They may eat it just as they would eat a gazelle or a deer.
passages.original: בִּשְׁעָרֶ֖יךָ תֹּאכֲלֶ֑נּוּ הַטָּמֵ֤א וְהַטָּהוֹר֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו כַּצְּבִ֖י וְכָאַיָּֽל׃

passages.text: But you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to Israel.
Do not eat the blood of the animal.
Pour the blood on the ground.
Pour it out like water.
passages.original: רַ֥ק אֶת־ דָּמ֖וֹ לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑ל עַל־ הָאָ֥רֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶ֖נּוּ כַּמָּֽיִם׃פ
